name: backdoor-firewall-rule
description: Practice-box misconfiguration: adds an attacker-style iptables INPUT ACCEPT rule for an outside source IP on a TCP management port, both to the live ruleset and persisted to /etc/iptables/rules.v4. The live rule is what the paired command_json check scores (hardened = source IP absent from the whole ruleset and rules.v4); the persisted file doubles as the forensics breadcrumb. Vars: SOURCE_IP (required), DST_PORT (required). Use an RFC 5737 TEST-NET address so the planted rule can never actually admit traffic.
script:
#!/bin/sh
# backdoor-firewall-rule -- plants an attacker-style firewall allowlist rule:
# an ACCEPT for an outside source IP on a management port, added to the LIVE
# iptables ruleset AND persisted to /etc/iptables/rules.v4 (so it survives a
# reboot once netfilter-persistent/iptables-persistent is installed, and so
# the persisted file is a forensics artifact even before that).
#
# Vars: SOURCE_IP (required, e.g. the attacker's documentation-ONLY address);
# DST_PORT (required). Idempotent: -C guards the live rule and the rules.v4
# write is a fixed fresh file. NOTE: writing rules.v4 fresh is intentional --
# practice boxes plant this before teams touch the box; never run it on a box
# whose rules.v4 you care about.
set -eu

: "${SOURCE_IP:?SOURCE_IP is required}"
: "${DST_PORT:?DST_PORT is required}"

if ! iptables -C INPUT -p tcp -s "$SOURCE_IP" --dport "$DST_PORT" -j ACCEPT 2>/dev/null; then
    iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s "$SOURCE_IP" --dport "$DST_PORT" -j ACCEPT
fi

mkdir -p /etc/iptables
cat > /etc/iptables/rules.v4 <<RULES
*filter
:INPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:FORWARD ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -p tcp -s $SOURCE_IP --dport $DST_PORT -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
RULES
